rule: mixed: this line is context only and is never parsed - the rule reaches the knowledge base only through the four sentences below. Both rule-bearing sentences (t1, t2) do produce rules that fire, but each loses part of the link between the shielding and its effect, and neither can express "through winter" as a whole-season extent. t3 is clean; t4 needs one small change. Apply the rewrites below and the rule is well covered.
texts: bad: two things go wrong. "Shield a cove from north winds" put the winds in the spatial origin slot - the parse now reads as though something came from the north winds, rather than that the cove is protected against them - and the resulting burning is keyed to the cove rather than to each shielding, so two shieldings of one cove collapse into a single burn event. Rewrite as: "Whenever cliff-spires shield a cove against north winds, the lanterns in that cove burn stably throughout winter." Note that "through/throughout winter" can still only be recorded as a point in time - the whole-season extent has no representation yet, and no wording of yours can fix that.

mixed: the rule fires and most of the sentence is handled well (the by-phrase agent, "from the north wind" as a plain circumstance rather than a place, and "stay lit" as a continuing state), but the derived lit-state is left with no link at all back to the blocking that licenses it, so nothing records that the lanterns stay lit while the cove is blocked. Rewrite with an explicit occurrence and an active condition clause: "Whenever cliff-spires block a cove from the north wind, the lanterns in that cove stay lit throughout winter." "Through winter" still cannot be recorded as a whole-season extent - a known gap, not something your wording causes.

good. fully faithful, no adjudication needed: one name symbol for Northcove with its "is a cove" typing stated separately, "shielded" as its own property rather than fused into the kind, and Aelmere recorded as containing it.

mixed: the never-rule fires and "never" is recorded correctly, but "in cold winds" was read as a place - the parse says the lanterns are located inside the winds rather than that cold winds are the circumstance under which they never fail. Give the circumstance its own finite clause: "When cold winds blow, Northcove lanterns never go out."
